bullets.title: MSFT: Citi raises PT to $636 on Azure/CoPilot acceleration; CIO survey confirms AI leadership
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy and raises MSFT PT to $636 (~23x FY29 PE) on expected ~2pt Azure beat in FQ1 (implying 46-47% YoY CC acceleration) and strong CoPilot net adds (+9M expected). CIO survey shows MSFT as clear leader in AI spending share gains, with resellers reporting 5pt q/q uptick in NTM sales growth to 16%. Azure targeted to exit F4Q at 48%+ growth; FY27 CapEx guide expected $60B+ with Citi full-year estimate at $237B vs Street $220B.

bullets.title: META: Citi raises PT to $895; Muse drops to #2 App Store behind chicken promotion
bullets.body: Citi raises META PT to $895 from $800 on clearer product roadmap and updated FY27 expense outlook, with 3Q revenues tracking +25% y/y ex-FX. On the product front, META Muse briefly dropped to #2 on the US App Store behind a Dave's Hot Chicken free-slider promotion — though Raymond James sees Muse as a structural threat to subscription businesses (CHTR/CMCSA most at risk; NFLX/SPOT relatively insulated with ~2% monthly churn).

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini 4 Argon ties GPT-6 at 60% cost; GCP +91% y/y projected; Canada cloud deal at risk
bullets.body: Google's Gemini 4 Argon rolled out globally, matching GPT-6 Astra on the Intelligence Index at 60% of cost per task — prompting positive analyst sentiment ('Google is back'). Citi projects GCP +91% y/y on TPU sales with FY27 capex revised +60% y/y to $329.3B. Separately, Canada's government is hesitant to approve an already-signed GOOGL cloud computing deal amid the US-Canada trade war.

bullets.title: NVDA/MU: Musk praises MU pricing; Rubin unit estimates trimmed; AI de-grossing broadens
bullets.body: Elon Musk publicly praised Micron as 'reasonable' on future memory pricing while labeling rivals 'extortionate' — a potential positive signal for MU. Meanwhile, UBS trimmed Q4 Nvidia Rubin unit estimates to 1.6-1.8M from 2.1M, cutting KYEC Q4 guidance from +18% to +9% QoQ. Hedge fund AI de-grossing is broadening beyond semis with US Semis nets at 88th percentile, down from near 100th percentile last week.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS/IREN: Negative gamma cycle as converts trade below par; financing now the bottleneck
bullets.body: CRWV, NBIS, and IREN represent ~$30B of the $450B convertible bond market (7% of total convert issuance); CRWV's converts are trading below par with unsecured notes at ~15% yield (1000bps spread-to-worst). Simultaneous declines in bonds and equities are creating a negative gamma dynamic as shorts press — CRWV -7.6% premarket, NBIS -6.0%, IREN broader weakness. Street is positioning for a capex cycle pullback; NVDA owns 11% of CRWV and has expressed willingness to absorb excess capacity.

bullets.title: NOW: Citi raises PT to $170; denies Decagon M&A; Stagwell 3-yr collaboration announced
bullets.body: Citi raises NOW PT to $170 from $154 (Buy) on stabilizing AI SKU adoption and federal cyber demand pickup. NOW separately denied Decagon M&A interest, saying its organic growth profile has no major gaps requiring a large acquisition. Stagwell also announced a three-year marketing modernization collaboration with ServiceNow.

bullets.title: ACN: +3.6% premarket on first analyst day since 2022; targets MSD-HSD revenue growth through FY29
bullets.body: Accenture held its first analyst day since 2022, targeting mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth for FY27-29 (above Street) with +10-30bps margin expansion and FCF/NI >=1.1x. UBS sees FY28-29 growth at +6% vs Street +4.8%. Early investor pushback centers on a significant FCF decline in FY28 (~18% below Street projections). ACN was +2.7% in pre-market.

bullets.title: IBM: Citi maintains Buy ahead of 10/21 earnings; Q4 mainframe redemption the key re-rating catalyst
bullets.body: Citi expects IBM to report in-line Q3 results on 10/21 with reiterated FY26 guidance, and sees modest upside to PTIM/FCFM from org efficiency. The key re-rating catalyst is Q4 mainframe redemption potential from on-prem renaissance and hybrid workload repatriation in the AI infra buildout climate; 75% of ~$700M deal-slippage seen recaptured by year-end. Red Hat can modestly accelerate on OpenShift share gains post-VMware price hikes.

bullets.title: TXN: JPM buyside survey ahead of Oct 21 earnings; F3Q26 guide range $5.65-6.15B
bullets.body: JPMorgan is surveying buyside on TXN's F3Q26 print (earnings call Oct 21 at 4:30pm ET). Survey expectations: revenue guide $5.65-6.15B, OPM ~44%, EPS $2.23-2.57; F4Q26 consensus at $5.71B revenue/$2.25 EPS. One key question: whether TXN can broadly increase 2027 pricing. Separately, Citi sees TXN as among the best-positioned analog names for 800VDC data center power architecture adoption beginning 2H27.

bullets.title: AMAT: Sells off 7.6% post-Analyst Day; margin/WFE share targets disappoint vs. buyside
bullets.body: AMAT fell ~7.6% in a sell-the-news reaction after guiding to 500bps gross margin expansion by 2030 and ~1000bps OPM improvement — viewed as insufficient vs. buyside hopes for earlier achievement. WFE market share target of ~2ppt gain through 2030 was deemed unexciting. Citi maintains Buy but acknowledges the messaging failed to spark interest despite WFE consensus estimates of $225-250B in 2027.

bullets.title: BE: $4B, 702MW AEP fuel cell deal for Google in Wyoming confirmed; full ops by end-2028
bullets.body: Bloom Energy and AEP announced a 702MW fuel cell project near Cheyenne for Google under a 20-year PPA, valued at ~$4B; construction starts 2026 with full operations by end-2028 to qualify for tax credits. This leaves ~200MW remaining on the AEP framework. OPCO notes concerns on stack life warranty reserves but views the deal as significant validation.

bullets.title: ORCL: Project Jupiter pipeline FERC approval expedited; in-service slipped to Feb 2027
bullets.body: Oracle is requesting FERC expedite approval of the 18-mile Green Chile gas pipeline for its Project Jupiter AI Data Center; in-service slipped to Feb 2027. ORCL expects no FY27 impact from the delay and is providing further updates at its Oct 28 Investor Day. Project Jupiter construction is progressing with power and regulatory challenges actively being addressed.

bullets.title: NFLX: Cuts ~6% of staff (~1,000 positions), largest reduction since 2022
bullets.body: Netflix is cutting approximately 6% of its workforce (~1,000 positions), per media reports, following an early October Puck News report indicating ~5% planned layoffs. Hedgeye's Risk Range Signals flag NFLX as bearish trend. No specifics on which business units are affected.

bullets.title: BKNG: Launches Vayo AI travel agent with $100M investment
bullets.body: Booking Holdings announced a $100M investment in new company Vayo, a personal AI travel agent launching in private beta targeting frequent travelers. Planned features include direct booking, a native app, and multi-user trip planning. Vayo accesses only travel confirmations and keeps the rest of users' inboxes private.

bullets.title: RBLX: DA Davidson raises PT to $50 (Neutral); DAU upside in 2H27 if GTA VI doesn't cannibalize
bullets.body: DA Davidson raised RBLX PT from $40 to $50 (Neutral), citing mid-to-high-teens DAU growth potential in 2H27 as comparisons ease and age verification progresses. The key risk is GTA VI (Nov 19 launch) and discovery algorithm changes — consensus estimates have reset lower, creating upside opportunity if those headwinds don't materialize. Roth Capital is separately publishing a proprietary cohort survey on Roblox engagement and spend by age group.

bullets.title: IONQ: Jefferies Buy/$80 PT; stock -5.3% premarket on $2B equity offering
bullets.body: IonQ is down 5.3% in pre-market trading following a $2B equity offering announcement. Jefferies maintains a Buy rating with an $80 price target, noting IonQ's trapped-ion technology for scalable quantum systems accessible via AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Market cap is ~$15.7B.

bullets.title: SHOP: Bullish signals — up 1.7% daily, +18.7% over 52 weeks; KeyBanc AI spend tailwind thesis
bullets.body: Shopify was flagged at 52-week highs on the Canadian exchange (+18.7% over 52 weeks, +1.7% daily). KeyBanc separately identifies SHOP as positioned for further growth with accelerating AI adoption, consistent with the broader market voice view of SHOP alongside CRWD, SNOW, and PLTR as AI software beneficiaries.

bullets.title: HPE/DELL: Both downgraded by Barclays; -5.2% and -3.7% premarket respectively
bullets.body: Barclays downgraded both HPE and DELL, sending shares -5.2% and -3.7% respectively in pre-market trading. No detailed rationale provided in the items beyond the broader semiconductor/AI hardware sector weakness narrative and elevated earnings expectations.

bullets.title: RH: Reduced fall discounts from 70% to 50% (vs. 60% last year); Hedgeye bullish near-term
bullets.body: RH trimmed its fall sale discount from 70% (where it started this year) to 50% as of Oct 16, versus 60% last year — signaling reduced promotional intensity. Hedgeye expects sales, EBIT, and cash flow to accelerate this quarter before a potential inflation/rates leg down in April 2027, with the core business supporting $35-$40 standalone stock value.

bullets.title: QBTS/RGTI/OKLO/UEC: Universe names hitting 52-week lows amid broad tech/energy weakness
bullets.body: Multiple universe names are at 52-week lows: QBTS (D-Wave) down 68.7% YTD, RGTI (Rigetti) down 77.9% YTD, OKLO down 82.3% YTD, and UEC (Uranium Energy) down 48.7% YTD. The quantum computing and nuclear/uranium names have been among the worst performers in the broader AI infrastructure de-grossing cycle.
